name: Sitio Historico (Centro Historico)
tagline: Colourful UNESCO old town on the hills
description: The historic heart of Olinda, a UNESCO-listed cluster of pastel colonial houses, baroque churches, convents and ateliers along steep cobbled lanes, crowned by the Alto da Se hill with its cathedral and sweeping sea and city views.
bestFor: Culture lovers, artists and slow travellers wanting atmosphere over convenience and speed

name: Carmo and Varadouro
tagline: Lower historic streets near the sea
description: The lower districts fringing the old town, home to the landmark Carmo church and the flatter Varadouro area, blending heritage character with everyday local life, markets and easier walking access down toward the waterfront and main roads.
bestFor: Those wanting old-town charm with flatter streets and daily local amenities nearby

name: Bairro Novo (Beachfront)
tagline: Relaxed seafront away from old town
description: Olinda's beachfront district stretching along the coast, offering a calmer, more residential feel with a seaside avenue, simpler modern flats, bars and easy access to sand, appealing to those who prefer ocean breezes over cobbled hills.
bestFor: Beach lovers seeking cheaper flats, sea air and a quieter everyday pace

name: Casa Caiada (toward Recife)
tagline: Modern side bridging Olinda and Recife
description: A more modern, built-up district on the Recife-facing side of Olinda, with taller buildings, supermarkets, services and quick transport links, suiting nomads who want everyday convenience and an easy commute to Recife's coworking and amenities.
bestFor: Practical residents prioritising amenities and easy access to Recife's offices and shopping
